cells.tense: You are right here in it, and the spark is landing where you meant it to.
cells.ask: Teach one thing you just figured out to someone who has never heard it — out loud, today, no slides, no plan.
cells.core:
You start things and you mean them. The confidence is not put on — it grew from something you actually found, which is why it carries. What you bring gets into the shared story because you bring it ready and let it be seen.

Going well, this looks like saying what you are learning while it is still wet, before it hardens into a position, and the room takes it in and adds to it. The meaning gets passed on because you kept it alive instead of polished. Watch the moment when the fire is young and the pull is to hold it close. Handing it over early is how it grows.
cells.sheetLine: You start fires that get taken up and carried on.
cells.verb: Starting fires with nothing but enthusiasm and direction
cells.place: The living room where a group's shared story is kept and passed on

cells.tense: You are already living past the launch, running at the moment they finally get it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are about to announce and sit on it a day. Let someone else speak first in the next room you walk into.
cells.core:
There is a version of this ahead where the whole room gets it, and you are sprinting toward that version while they walk. Each conversation turns into a chance to bring them there. The sprint is eating the thing it was for — shared meaning only forms when people arrive on their own feet.

Going well, the fire spreads because it was given time and air, not because it was shoved. What you are reaching for is already catching somewhere in the room; you just cannot see it from inside the run. Slow down enough to notice, and the next step will show itself without your hand on it.
cells.sheetLine: You are pushing the spark instead of letting it catch.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, match in hand, unlit.
cells.ask: Tell one person one true thing you are excited about, badly, without turning it into a plan. Then stop.
cells.core:
The enthusiasm has not gone anywhere. It stopped coming out, and the room you are in has nothing new from you in it. You are not empty — the offering stopped, and not offering became the habit. The shared story keeps going, but your part of it has gone quiet.

Going well looks like handing over the smallest version, before it is ready, to one person. The response teaches you more than the waiting does. What is missing is not the spark. It is the small act of saying it out loud while it is still rough and letting someone else take it from there.
cells.sheetLine: The spark is still there. The offering stopped.

cells.tense: You are already lighting this room and describing it as if it happened on its own.
cells.ask: Name one thing you started that others now carry — say it out loud as yours, once, without softening it.
cells.core:
You begin things here — in how you ask, what you pick up, what you let stand. The room is shaped by it. Then you describe it as if it were that way from the start, or as if the thing did it by itself. The starting is yours. The saying-so is not.

Going well, this looks like owning one thing plainly, without making it a speech. Not louder — claimed. That is the difference between being part of the story and knowing you hold the pen. The fire is already lit. Put your name on the match, once, and let it stand.
cells.sheetLine: The room is already yours. Say so out loud.
